newsitem.title: USA: Irvine Sensors sees Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: Irvine Sensors sees Q4 loss.

text.p: John Stuart, chief financial officer of Irvine Sensors Corp, said in a statement on Wednesday that operating losses in the fourth quarter had grown, and that the company would post a bigger net loss for the period than in the third quarter of 1996.
"Losses from operations widened during the fourth fiscal quarter ended September 29, primarily as a result of declining margins and delays in government procurements," he said.
The company reported a loss of $3.15 million, or $0.19 per share, in the third quarter of this year.
Stuart said fourth-quarter revenues were more than double those of both the prior quarter and last year's fourth fiscal quarter, but did not approach levels anticipated earlier in the year.
"This has resulted in an expected loss in the fourth quarter greater than that of the preceding third fiscal quarter," he said.

"We have been concerned about government delays since the historic budget battle at the start of the fiscal year, but the extent of the margin pressure is likely to continue or even increase with the recent collapse in DRAM prices.

"Furthermore, the accelerated availability of 64 Mb DRAMs in response to this price decline may increase competition for our current generation of DRAM products. We are evaluating our product mix to respond to this market shift," he said.
